correctness.rationale: The prefix automaton has only i->j with j<=i+1 and A_{i,i+1}=pi(w_{i+1}); absorbing edge is from m-1 via w_m. A specified inverse matrix entry has a unique lower-triangular cofactor, giving E z^(T-m)=p_w/det(I-zA). A^m row sums <=1-p_w, hence rho(A)<1, normalization det(I-A)=p_w. Matrix log identity gives nonnegative Levy masses tr(A^k)/k summing to -log(p_w). The ordinary cumulant formula follows by spectral exponential decay. Tested 498 patterns with independent rational verification and brute enumeration; bounded checks do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected the 2022 arXiv paper, the relevant 2014 full open-access article sections, and the full author-uploaded 2010 paper. Repeated-success waiting-time PGFs, finite-Markov-chain embedding algorithms for general patterns, and compound-Poisson approximations for pattern counts do not directly assert the all-word exact first-wait compound-Poisson decomposition. Completed semantic database/literature searches and comparison with relevant published mathematical claims found no equivalent or stronger claim. Uninspected earlier pattern-generating-function sources remain a specified risk.
residual_risks: Classic pattern first-passage literature may call the same conclusion compound-geometric, logarithmic combinatorial or renewal representations rather than infinite divisibility.
The finite Markov determinant identity itself is elementary from standard embeddings; originality is specifically the universal nonnegative trace Levy measure and first-wait CP conclusion.
Published-search and mathematical-record coverage is finite; no independent literature audit.

Additional historical works on word-pattern generating functions (such as Fu and Chang 2002 and Antzoulakos 2001) were not inspected sequentially in full and may contain a differently framed equivalent assertion.

value.rationale: Universal exact compound-Poisson representation for arbitrary single-pattern excess waiting times supplies jump masses, infinite divisibility, all cumulants, and an explicit simulation law. This structural property is stronger than raw recurrence coefficients, not automatically true for arbitrary phase-type stopping times, and applies to overlap-sensitive, nonuniform finite-alphabet patterns. It is motivated by classical run and word-wait distributions, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
